title: Keeping Data Centers Cool, Efficient and Resilient with Smarter Flow Monitoring
summary: See how ultrasonic and electromagnetic flow meters support efficient data center cooling, reliable operations and proactive system monitoring.
body_markdown:
Data centers are the physical infrastructure behind the internet and have experienced rapid recent growth driven by artificial intelligence, cloud computing and general digital expansion. The United States leads the global data center market, with more than 4,000 operational facilities and major concentrations in Virginia, Texas and California, according to[Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1662630/us-number-of-data-centers-by-state/) .


As the need for data centers continues to grow, these facilities are becoming larger and more energy-intensive. Housing the equipment and servers that keep digital services running around the clock, they require huge amounts of electricity to meet their operational demands. Operating 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, data centers generate significant heat and rely on vast cooling systems to prevent overheating, maintain uptime and protect critical infrastructure.


## Optimizing Data Center Cooling


Cooling is essential to data center management and facilities would not be able to operate without effective cooling systems in place. Cooling is essential to maintaining data center uptime and reliability. Depending on the facility and cooling architecture, thermal management systems can represent 30-50% of total energy consumption and may require substantial water resources, creating both operational and sustainability challenges.


Due to growing environmental concerns, data centers are under mounting pressure to operate in a more sustainable manner. In the United States, data centers face environmental rules primarily handled at state and local levels and while there is no single comprehensive federal standard, operators must comply with a mix of federal environmental statutes and local mandates and increasingly provide detailed reports on water and energy consumption.


To maintain compliance with emerging and changing regulations, facility managers are increasingly looking for cost-effective and efficient ways to enhance operational performance. By utilizing real-time data to track coolant distribution, prevent over-pumping, and detect early anomalies, flow monitoring technology can significantly optimize data center cooling systems and deliver many benefits. Flow monitors give facility managers the ability to:


- Track the distribution of chilled water to verify server racks receive adequate coolant flow.
- Detect system blockages, flow anomalies and leaks ahead of time before they trigger catastrophic server shutdowns.
- Maintain system efficiency by combining flow rate data with temperature fluctuations to calculate exact thermal energy removal (kW or BTU).
- Conserve energy by automatically scaling pump speeds up or down to match processing loads.
- Conserve water by measuring the exact amount of makeup water needed to replace cooling water evaporation and blowdown.
- Generate the auditable data needed to meet strict environmental and local permitting mandates required for regulatory compliance.


## Flow Monitoring Solutions for Data Center Applications


Continuous evaluation of flow provides real-time, accurate and reliable data, giving valuable insight into system integrity to optimize performance and efficiency and reduce operating costs. For data center operators, integrating flow meters within chiller networks is often an effective and straightforward way to enhance operations. With a variety of flow monitoring technologies available, data centers of all sizes can find solutions to meet their individual application needs.


Using Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction to measure liquid velocity, electromagnetic flow meters are a popular choice. With no moving parts, they offer a low-maintenance solution that delivers high accuracy and reliability. Able to accurately measure conductive liquids such as water-glycol mixes, they are well suited to chiller skids, cooling distribution units (CDUs), and are often used in large chilled or condenser main pipes as they cause zero pressure drop.


Ultrasonic clamp-on flow meters are a versatile solution for both retrofit installations and new construction projects. Installed without the need to cut through pipes and shut down cooling systems and active server racks, these meters operate by sending high-frequency sound waves through pipes to measure fluid speed without causing blockages or drops in pressure. Offering impressive accuracy, simple installation and non-invasive operation, this technology is suited to main chilled water headers, large pipes and deionized water loops where mechanical parts or low conductivity may otherwise cause issues.

## Real-Time Flow Monitoring Success Stories


For one large data center in the United States, verifying that their chiller supply and return lines were completely full was a key factor in optimizing operations and improving performance. Partial filling or “not-full pipe” conditions can affect cooling capacity, equipment reliability and measurement accuracy and operators were keen to avoid this.


Using the[Dynasonics® TFX-5000 Ultrasonic Clamp-on Flow Meter](https://www.badgermeter.com/products/meters/ultrasonic/tfx-5000-ultrasonic-clamp-on-flow-meter/) , operators gained an accurate and reliable flow monitoring solution that could also verify when pipes were only partially filled. By installing the transducers on top of the pipe, the system could accurately identify not-full-pipe conditions and, when configured with a communications output, send an alarm to the PLC, allowing proactive management of emerging issues to avoid catastrophic system failures. Highly efficient and simple to install, this delivers a state-of-the-art solution to optimize system performance and extend equipment longevity.


In another US-based data center, operators needed a precise, real-time monitoring solution that could provide continuous and accurate measurement of water flow in the chiller system's supply and return lines. With dense, heat-intensive computing loads running 24/7, operators needed to maintain effective cooling and quickly identify flow discrepancies to verify the correct distribution of chilled water throughout the system. Delivering real-time flow data, the[ModMAG® M2000 Electromagnetic Flow Meter](https://www.badgermeter.com/products/meters/electromagnetic/m2000-electromagnetic-flow-meter/) provided a leading-edge solution that enabled operators to maintain stable thermal conditions and prevent unplanned outages. Offering seamless integration into building management systems, accuracy of ±1% and a zero straight run requirement for applications with limited space. This enhanced flow monitoring solution gave operators the ability to continually track flow rates and proactively manage emerging issues. Complete system oversight means that flow variations are immediately identified, leading to increased system efficiency, reduced operating costs and improved sustainability.
